# Map.set benchmark

## Pull Request by @mateuszsikora

I added a benchmark that checks if it is worth to check if an item exists in the map or simply override it.

## Walkthrough

A new benchmark suite was added to evaluate and compare two strategies for updating values in a JavaScript Map. The suite consists of two tests: one that uses two get operations with a conditional set, and another that uses a single get followed by an unconditional set. Benchmark results are saved in a new JSON file, documenting the performance outcomes of both approaches. No existing code or exported entities were modified; only new files were introduced for benchmarking purposes.

## Changes

| File(s)                                              | Change Summary                                                                                                      |
|------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| benchmarks/collections/map-set.ts                    | Added a new benchmark suite comparing two Map update strategies: "2 gets + conditional set" vs "1 get 1 set".      |
| benchmarks/collections/expected/map-set.json         | Added a benchmark result file recording performance metrics for the two Map update strategies.                      |

## Comment by @coderabbitai[bot]

_⚠️ Potential issue_

**First benchmark may not be testing what was intended.**

The benchmark name suggests testing a conditional set pattern, but due to JavaScript's object reference behavior, the code has an issue:

1. In the first iteration, `map.get(key)` returns `undefined`, so `initialValue` is used
2. `value.counter` is updated (modifying the `initialValue` object)
3. `map.set(key, value)` is called only on the first iteration
4. In subsequent iterations, the `map.has(key)` check prevents `map.set` from being called again

After the first iteration, you're just modifying the existing object by reference without calling `map.set` again, which doesn't accurately test the intended pattern.


A more accurate implementation would create a new object for each update:

```diff
  function conditionalSet(i: number) {
    const value = map.get(key) ?? initialValue;
-   value.counter += i;
+   const newValue = { counter: value.counter + i };
    if (!map.has(key)) {
-     map.set(key, value);
+     map.set(key, newValue);
+   } else {
+     map.set(key, newValue);
    }
  }
```


<!-- suggestion_start -->

`````suggestion
      function conditionalSet(i: number) {
        const value = map.get(key) ?? initialValue;
        const newValue = { counter: value.counter + i };
        if (!map.has(key)) {
          map.set(key, newValue);
        } else {
          map.set(key, newValue);

`````
